rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose everyday way to say that you can tell two things apart.

example.english: Can you discriminate between the tastes of these two teas?
example.traditional: 你分得出呢兩種茶嘅味道嗎？
example.jyutping: nei5 fan1 dak1 ceot1 ni1 loeng5 zung2 caa4 ge3 mei6 dou6 maa3

rows.note: Use this when treating people differently has the negative sense of prejudice or unfairness.

example.english: Companies shouldn't discriminate against people based on gender.
example.traditional: 公司唔應該因為性別而歧視人。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 m4 jing1 goi1 jan1 wai6 sing3 bit6 ji4 kei4 si6 jan4

rows.note: Use this for the neutral sense of treating different people or groups differently according to their traits or circumstances.

example.english: Teachers discriminate between students according to their needs.
example.traditional: 老師會按學生嘅需要分別對待佢哋。
example.jyutping: lou5 si1 wui5 on3 hok6 saang1 ge3 seoi1 jiu3 fan1 bit6 deoi3 doi6 keoi5 dei6
